title: The design process
examples: What is the difference between a design brief and a specification?
How many times should I iterate on a design?
Can you give me an example of a good design brief?

explain.say: Today we are learning about the design process for making things.
First we start with a design brief to understand the problem.
Next we write a specification to make our goals very clear.

items: Must be | At least 10 cm long

explain.say: Iteration means repeating the design process to make it better.
For a real life example think about designing a phone case.
A common mistake is forgetting to test your first idea.

faq.q: What is the difference between a brief and a spec?
faq.a: The brief explains the problem and who it is for. The specification turns those ideas into measurable details.
asks: What should I write in the brief?
Is the spec just a list of things?

faq.q: How many times should I iterate?
faq.a: There is no fixed number, but you should keep iterating until the design meets all its specifications.
asks: When do I know I am finished?
Does iteration mean I have to make a new thing?

faq.q: Do I need to use specific materials in my brief?
faq.a: Sometimes the brief will give you material limits, like only using recycled plastic.

faq.q: If my first prototype fails, is that bad?
faq.a: No, failing is just information that tells you what to change next in your iteration.
asks: Is failure part of the process?
What if my first idea is bad?

faq.q: What is the most important part of the design process?
faq.a: Understanding the user's needs from the brief is the most important starting point.

facts: A design brief defines the problem that needs solving.
A specification lists measurable requirements for the final product.
Iteration involves repeating design steps based on testing feedback.
The process moves from understanding to creating to improving.

quiz.say: A designer writes down that the object must hold a book and weigh less than one kilogram. This is part of the:
quiz.why: The specification makes the general idea measurable and definite.

wrong.1: The brief explains the general need, not the exact weight limit.
wrong.2: Iteration is the act of repeating the design, not writing the rules.
wrong.3: A prototype is the physical model, not the written rules.

quiz.say: After building a first model, the designer asks friends what they think of it. This action is part of:
quiz.why: Getting feedback and making changes based on it is the core of iteration.

wrong.1: The specification is the plan, not the act of testing the plan.
wrong.2: The brief is written at the very beginning, before testing.
wrong.3: A concept is the initial idea, not the repeated improvement cycle.

quiz.say: If a design needs to be used by children aged five to eight, which document must the designer focus on first?
quiz.why: The brief tells you about the user and the problem, which is the first step.

wrong.0: A prototype is the physical result, not the initial understanding.
wrong.2: The specification measures things, but the brief tells you who it is for.
wrong.3: Iteration happens after you already have an idea to test.
